content.value_statement: Avalonia teams need consistent ViewModel, command, navigation, and wizard patterns. This skill provides focused Zafiro and ReactiveUI guidance for maintainable MVVM applications.
actual_capabilities: Explains ReactiveUI ViewModel patterns using ReactiveObject, reactive properties, and WhenAnyValue transformations.
Shows how to create and enhance commands with IEnhancedCommand and ReactiveCommand.
Guides construction of multi-step flows with SlimWizard and WizardBuilder.
Describes section-based navigation using INavigator and Section attributes.
Documents ViewModel-to-view mapping and dependency registration through a CompositionRoot.
limitations: Does not generate a complete Avalonia project structure by itself.
Assumes the application already uses Zafiro, ReactiveUI, and compatible source generators.
Provides pattern guidance, not exhaustive API reference documentation.
Examples are conceptual and may need adaptation for each application architecture.

use_cases.title: Standardize MVVM Implementation
use_cases.description: Apply consistent ReactiveUI and Zafiro conventions across ViewModels, properties, subscriptions, and commands.

use_cases.title: Design Guided Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan multi-step wizard flows with validation, custom next commands, final steps, and navigation integration.

use_cases.title: Review Application Composition
use_cases.description: Check ViewModel registration, section discovery, view mapping, and CompositionRoot responsibilities before scaling the app.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic ViewModel
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a reactive screen model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a simple Avalonia ViewModel with ReactiveUI properties, validation state, and one enhanced submit command.

prompt_templates.title: Add Section Navigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate navigation and modular UI work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to convert an Avalonia screen into a Zafiro navigation section with a Section attribute and INavigator-based transitions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Wizard Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow design with multiple steps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a SlimWizard flow for onboarding, including step ViewModels, validation gates, custom commands, and final completion behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an MVVM Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of composition and lifecycle patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Avalonia MVVM architecture for command handling, disposables, section discovery, view mapping, and dependency registration.

output_examples.input: Design a ViewModel for a form with a name field and a submit action.
output: A recommended ViewModel structure using reactive properties for input and busy state.
A command design that supports asynchronous submission and clear command text.
A cleanup note for subscriptions and command error handling.

output_examples.input: Plan a three-step project creation wizard for an Avalonia app.
output: A step-by-step wizard outline with initial data entry, validation, review, and completion.
Navigation rules for next, back, and final completion behavior.
Guidance on where each step ViewModel should own state and validation.

output_examples.input: Review how my app wires views, ViewModels, and sections together.
output: A composition checklist covering service registration, section discovery, and view location.
Recommendations for transient and singleton ViewModel lifetimes.
Warnings about mixing manual view creation with dependency injection.

best_practices: Keep ViewModels reactive, disposable, and focused on state transformation rather than view creation.
Use enhanced commands with clear names, progress behavior, and centralized error handling.
Register navigation sections and ViewModel mappings consistently through the CompositionRoot.
anti_patterns: Putting navigation, validation, persistence, and view creation into one large ViewModel.
Creating ReactiveUI subscriptions without disposing them through a CompositeDisposable.
Hardcoding wizard step transitions where WizardBuilder rules would be clearer and safer.

faq.question: What framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Avalonia applications that use Zafiro and ReactiveUI for MVVM, navigation, commands, and wizards.

faq.question: Can this skill create a full application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture and implementation guidance for ViewModels, commands, sections, composition, and wizard flows.

faq.question: Does it require ReactiveUI.SourceGenerators?
faq.answer: The examples reference source-generator attributes for concise properties, but projects can adapt the patterns to manual ReactiveUI properties.

faq.question: How does it help with commands?
faq.answer: It explains when to use ReactiveCommand, how to enhance commands, and how to route command errors to UI services.

faq.question: How does it handle navigation?
faq.answer: It describes INavigator usage, section attributes, automatic section registration, and shell-level section switching.

faq.question: Is the skill safe to use?
faq.answer: The reviewed files contain documentation examples only. No malicious instructions or executable automation were found during audit.
